newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 13.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Monday:
* Indonesian government plans to invest up to $8 billion to build two research and development sites in West Java to boost the country's electronics exports, Bisnis Indonesia reported.

* The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished on Friday with a gain of 78.12 points at 6,703.79 as investors snapped up bargains after a massive sell-off sparked by surprisingly robust U.S. jobs growth in December.
* The Jakarta Composite Index rose 0.44 points, or 0.07 percent, to close at 657.87 points on Friday after coming under pressure from profit-taking during the afternoon session.
* On Monday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,364.10/64.00 in early trading against the opening of 2,363.50/64.00.
* Bimantara on strikes in South Korea which could have an impact on its automotive division. Bimantara had a link-up with Hyundai Motor Co Ltd.
* Telkom following reports it planned to launch several new business services in the middle of 1997.
* Fishing firm Daya Guna Samudera on expected higher demand from its main market Japan following reports of the oil tanker disaster there polluting fisheries areas.
* Texmaco Perkasa on reports the Texmaco Group planned to build a textile factory in East Timor.
* Cement firms Indocement, Semen Cibinong and Semen Gresik on a government announcement it would grant export licences to five cement manufacturers.
* Steady Safe on reports that a subsidiary has launched a ferry service plying the busy strait between Java and Sumatra islands.
